history.value: GV was founded in 2009 as Google Ventures by Bill Maris to invest Google's capital, and took the name GV in 2015 under Alphabet. Its bets include Uber, Nest, Slack and Flatiron Health. Led by David Krane, it invests from San Francisco, New York, Cambridge and London, and says it manages $13 billion.
history.basis: Founded as Google Ventures on March 31, 2009 by Bill Maris with an initial $100 million commitment from Google, renamed GV in December 2015 (Wikipedia, 'GV (company)', read 2026-09-29; the firm's own homepage caption 'EST. 2009'). Uber, Nest, Slack and Flatiron Health are on the firm's own list (gv.com/portfolio, with the firm's exit lines 'NYSE: UBER', 'Acquired by Google, 2014', 'NYSE: WORK', 'Acquired by Roche, 2018'). David Krane is 'CEO & Managing Partner' on the firm's team page (gv.com/team/david-krane). Offices: the firm's own offices document (San Francisco Bay Area as headquarters, New York, Cambridge, London). '$13B Under Management' is the firm's own stats box on gv.com (read 2026-09-29), stated as the firm's claim because no sworn figure exists (aum field). Moved to this sidecar, not the page: the vehicles by vintage (funds field), CapitalG and Gradient as separate Alphabet units, the $125 million European allocation of 2014 led by Tom Hulme, and Bill Maris's departure in 2016.

aum.basis: FIRM-STATED, both ends (Erik 2026-09-29, ruling decisions.md Delta 1): the firm's own '$13B Under Management' (gv.com stats box, read 2026-09-29), flagged firm_stated because no sworn figure exists. GV is a corporate venture arm and files no Form ADV: IAPD returns no firm under GV, GV Management, Google Ventures, Google or Alphabet (2026-09-29), so neither Item 5.F nor Section 7.B exists, and the vehicles raise no outside money (no fund Form D; the one Form D is GV 2025 GP, L.P., the team's own vehicle, $0 sold). Wikipedia's infobox says 'approximately $10 billion'. GV Management Company, L.L.C. (CIK 1940173) files 13F notices; its listed holdings are reported inside Alphabet Inc.'s 13F, which covers public equities only and is no AUM figure.

funds.basis: The GV vehicles on EDGAR (company search 'GV 20' and 'Google Ventures', 2026-09-29), newest first, vintage from the name, plus Google Ventures 2012, L.P., which filed nothing under its own name but is named in portfolio companies' filings (Upstart's 2020 S-1/A holder table, DocuSign's 2018 registration, Nextdoor's 2012 management rights letter). Sizes are null: Alphabet is the only limited partner, so no vehicle files a Form D or a Section 7.B gross asset value, and the firm publishes none. GV 2013, L.P. filed first as Google Ventures 2013, L.P. Not listed: GV 2025 GP, L.P. (CIK 2036706; its Form D reports 84 investors and $0 sold, the team's own general partner vehicle, evidence of a 2025 vintage whose fund entity is not on EDGAR), the GV 20xx GP entities, GV Management Company, L.L.C. (the manager), and CapitalG's vehicles (a separate firm). Press allocations: Google's commitment was $100 million in 2009 and $300 million a year from 2012 (Wikipedia); a $125 million European allocation was announced in 2014.

hq_location.basis: The firm's own site disagrees with the Form ADV principal office, None. GV files no Form ADV (decisions.md D1), so the rule's principal office does not exist. The firm's site labels its headquarters 'San Francisco Bay Area' (the Sanity offices document, read 2026-09-29), a region, and its own posts and bios place the Bay Area team in 'our San Francisco office' (Elena Sakach 2024-05-20, Michael McBride 2023-12-13, Brendan Bulik-Sullivan and Frederique Dame 2023-06-05) and 'our offices in San Francisco' (David Krane, 2026-02-02). The vehicles' filing address, 1600 Amphitheatre Parkway, Mountain View, is Alphabet's headquarters, not the firm's office. Rule (Erik 2026-09-24): the newest Form ADV principal office, unless the firm's own site disagrees, and then the site wins.

investment_scope.basis: focus from the firm's own site sector tags on 751 base rows, crosswalked to data/taxonomy/focus.json (crosswalk in config.json), published above 30 companies. Scope type is the curated judgement carried in investor.json.

investment_range.basis: MEDIAN $22.5M: the median entry round over the 78 members whose entry round is on EDGAR (the Form D round filed nearest the recorded entry date; p10 $6.5M, p25 $15.0M, p75 $50.0M, p90 $75.5M). LOWER and UPPER are the p10 and p90 of the same distribution, because the firm publishes no cheque range (the BCV convention). It is a round size, not a cheque size, and Form D coverage starts in 2009.

notable_investments.basis: The five best known of the firm's companies to a general reader, most recognised first (PRO-152, Erik 2026-09-24), each a member on the firm's own list: Uber (GV's 2013 investment), Stripe (a GV case study), Slack, Nest (bought by Google in 2014) and Robinhood. Left out as better known for other reasons: Waymo and Isomorphic Labs (Alphabet's own companies, decisions.md D4) and 23andMe.
